color_rules: Accent yellow is the logo yellow, sampled off the wordmark itself. The logo wins, per the rule this list used to carry while the hex was still provisional.
Every yellow surface carries ink text. Never white on yellow and never yellow on white at body size. Both fail WCAG AA.

Yellow on asphalt is the one place yellow may be decoration rather than action, because that is literally what the man paints. It is the wordmark, the painted lines and the section rules on dark bands, and nothing else.
On white sections yellow stays reserved for the primary action, unchanged.

Blue means ADA and nothing else. On a real lot the blue stall is the accessible stall, so the site uses blue the same way the pavement does. Dark bands use ada_on_dark because the white-surface blue fails contrast on asphalt.
Asphalt is a brand surface, not a dark mode. The wordmark is yellow on black, so the page alternates asphalt bands and white bands rather than sitting white throughout.
brand.reference_axis: From 1-800-STRIPER, the flat service grid where ADA sits at equal weight instead of buried, plus a quantified turnaround promise. From PMP, the client logo wall and the rating shown as a number. Both are structure, not look. Doctrine section 6, Rung 1 takes the axis and not the aesthetic.
brand.signature_element: A hand authored SVG of a real lot layout, stalls filling as the page scrolls, with the ADA stall and its access aisle in the blue. It doubles as the section progress indicator. It is meaningless for a competitor who is not leading on ADA, which is the test.
ai_tells_checked: No cream #F4F1EA background with high contrast serif and terracotta #D97757 accent
No near black background with a single acid green or vermilion accent
No broadsheet layout, hairline rules, zero radius dense columns
No 01 / 02 / 03 markers on anything that is not genuinely sequential
No gradient on a big number hero stat

body: Max Dyer started Kleen Stripe in Wichita in 1979 with one truck and one striping machine. There was no marketing to it. He striped a lot, the property manager next door saw it, and that was the next job.

Devin took it over in 2017. He is the third generation on the machine, and he still quotes the work himself, which means the person who tells you what it costs is the person who has to stand on the lot and do it. That arrangement keeps everybody honest.

The trade has changed in the ways that matter. ADA requirements got teeth, warehouses started wanting floors marked to the inch, and national franchises showed up in Wichita with call centers. What has not changed is that a lot either has straight lines on it or it does not, and you can see which from the street.

faqs.q: Do you have to close the whole lot?
faqs.a: No. Most jobs get done in sections so your tenants and customers keep parking. Each section needs to stay clear while the paint sets, and the crew works the sequence out with you before anybody puts a cone down.

faqs.q: Can you stripe over the old lines or does it need sealing first?
faqs.a: Either works. Striping over existing lines is the cheaper job and it looks fine when the asphalt underneath is sound. If the surface is oxidised and grey, the paint sits on top of loose material and it comes up early, so sealcoating first is the call. Devin tells you which one your lot is when he looks at it, and he will say so if the cheaper one is the right one.

services.name: ADA Compliance
services.title: ADA Parking Compliance in Kansas | Kleen Stripe
services.meta_description: ADA parking stalls, access aisles, signage and layouts for Kansas commercial properties. Get your lot walked and brought into compliance by Kleen Stripe.
services.lede: If you are on this page you are either coming off an inspection or you have a feeling about one. Either way, the lot is the part of an ADA complaint that is cheapest to fix and easiest to see from the parking area, which is why it is the part that gets cited.
body: Compliance is not just the blue paint. It is how many accessible stalls your total stall count requires, how wide the access aisle beside them is, whether one of them is van accessible, where the signs sit and how high they mount, the slope of the stall and the aisle, and whether somebody can get from that stall to your front door without leaving the accessible route.
Most lots that fail do not fail on the stall. They fail on the aisle, the sign height, or the route to the door. Those are the three the crew checks first.
scope: Accessible stall and access aisle layout to current standards
Van accessible stalls and the wider aisle they need
Accessible route from stall to entrance
ADA signage, supplied and installed at correct mounting height
Restriping existing accessible stalls that have faded or drifted
Walk the lot and tell you what is out, before you commit to anything
services.compliance_note: COPY GATE. Every dimension, ratio, slope figure and penalty amount on this page must be checked against the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design and any Kansas requirement before it is written. Do not write a number from memory and do not source one from a competitor's blog. DOJ civil penalty maximums adjust annually, so a figure without a current citation and date does not go on the page. Doctrine hard stop 1.

faqs.q: How many accessible stalls does my lot need?
faqs.needs: Requires the current ADA stall count table, verified against the 2010 Standards before this answer is written.

faqs.q: Can you tell me if my lot is out of compliance before I commit to anything?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is the usual way it starts. Devin walks it, tells you what is out and what it takes to fix, and you decide from there. There is no charge for being told your lot is fine.

services.why_own_page: Highest commercial intent term on the list, and the only one where the buyer is not shopping, they are exposed. PMP has no ADA page. EverLine handles it as a bullet inside a FAQ. This is the gap.
services.header_note: Blue field with white access-aisle hatching, per docs/design/direction-v2.html. On a real lot the hatched zone beside the accessible stall is the one you do not park in, so the page that sells compliance is drawn as that zone. Blue is used nowhere else on the site, which is what keeps this readable as a signal rather than decoration.

services.name: Sealcoating
services.title: Asphalt Sealcoating in Wichita, KS | Kleen Stripe
services.meta_description: Commercial asphalt sealcoating in Wichita and across Kansas. Protect the asphalt you already paid for before water gets into it. Quotes from Kleen Stripe.
services.lede: Asphalt fails from the top down and from the inside out at the same time. Sun oxidises the surface, water gets into what the sun opened up, and Kansas freezes it. Sealcoat is the layer that keeps that sequence from starting.
scope: Commercial lot sealcoating
Surface cleaning and prep before seal goes down
Oil spot priming
Crack sealing ahead of the seal coat
Restriping after the seal cures

faqs.q: How long does the lot need to stay closed?
faqs.needs: Devin's real cure window, question 14. Do not write a number here.

faqs.q: Do I need to restripe after sealcoating?
faqs.a: Yes. Seal goes over everything, so the lines go down again afterward. That is why the two get quoted together, and it is also the moment to fix a layout that was never right in the first place.

services.name: Crack Sealing and Pothole Repair
services.title: Crack Sealing & Pothole Repair, Wichita KS | Kleen Stripe
services.meta_description: Asphalt crack sealing and pothole repair for commercial lots in Wichita and across Kansas. Stop water getting under your asphalt. Kleen Stripe quotes.
services.lede: A crack is not a cosmetic problem, it is a door. Water goes through it, sits under the asphalt, freezes, and lifts the section from underneath. By the time you can see a pothole the damage happened a year earlier.
scope: Hot pour crack sealing
Pothole cut out and patch
Failed section repair
Concrete repair
Assessment of what needs sealing now and what can wait a season

faqs.q: Is patching worth it or should I just replace the section?
faqs.a: Depends what is under it. If the base is sound, a patch holds and you have bought years for a fraction of the cost. If the base has gone, a patch is a way of spending money twice. Devin will tell you which one you have, including when the answer is the expensive one.

faqs.a: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Older lots were often laid out generously, and the ADA stalls were added later by whoever had a brush. Devin measures it and tells you what the lot will actually hold, including when the answer is that it already holds it.

buyers.meta_description: Striping subcontractor for asphalt and concrete paving contractors and new construction in Wichita and across Kansas. On your schedule. Kleen Stripe.
buyers.h1: You laid it. He'll stripe it.
buyers.pain: Your striping sub is on the critical path at the exact point where everybody has already used up the float. What you need is somebody who shows up on the day and does not have to be chased.
body: Kleen Stripe subs striping to asphalt and concrete paving contractors and to new construction across Kansas. Layout from your drawings, ADA stalls to standard, fire lanes, and the markings the inspector is going to look for.
Send the plan and the date. If the date moves, say so and it moves.
proof_needed: Existing contractor relationships. Holland Paving and Wildcat Construction appear on his current site but need permission before they are named, question 11.

cta.label: Send a plan and a date

buyers.principle: Speed. They are on a deadline.

buyers.label: Small business owners
buyers.title: Small Business Parking Lot Striping | Wichita KS | Kleen Stripe
buyers.meta_description: Striping and sealcoating for small commercial lots in Wichita. A dozen stalls, a clear price and one day of work. Text a photo to Kleen Stripe for a number.
buyers.h1: A dozen stalls out front that nobody has touched in years
buyers.pain: You do not need a proposal. You need somebody to tell you what it costs to make the front of your business look like somebody owns it.
body: Small lots are a one day job and they are quoted the same way. Text a photograph and the address and you get a number, not a range and not a site visit you have to schedule around.
It is also the cheapest thing you will ever do to the outside of your building, which is worth knowing before you price a sign.
buyers.price_position_note: This is the one page where price-forward framing is defensible, per decision 2 option C. It stays off the homepage.

cta.label: Text a photo and get a number

This is a shared template, not per-city prose: only {{city}} and {{state}} vary, and the body restates facts already established elsewhere rather than inventing local detail (no landmarks, no job counts, no claims about work actually done in this city, since none of that exists yet). clients_note: Sourced from the client's own current site. All publishable false until Devin confirms per account. Several national accounts prohibit vendors from using their name or mark. A logo wall needs written permission, a text mention usually needs less, and a generic line naming no one needs none. Question 11.

Two files were excluded from this array and left out of public/photos/gallery/: a Kleen Stripe wordmark graphic on a black background (819b1bf9), which is brand art rather than a job photo, and an exact duplicate (ca2f9bdb, byte-identical to b20935af). Both remain in public/photos/source/ for the record. See the checkpoint report for the two photos flagged for a third-party naming risk and the two flagged for a baked-in UI artifact.

photo_assignments.note: hero changed from wide-lot-crosshatch-winter (white lines, visible cracks, dead winter brush, fought the site's own crack-sealing pitch and the accent palette) to sealcoat-apartments-fresh-lines: yellow paint on dark asphalt, the same colour doing the same job as the accent, no defects, and lines that recede toward the garage with a clean single vanishing point for the hero reveal animation to sweep along. trust is null on purpose. Nothing in the 16 photos clearly shows Devin or the crew as a person, only a partial POV shot of a foot and shadow (crew-operating-striper-pov). The work order says to leave the trust slot as a placeholder rather than substitute something that does not show what the slot promises, so it stays a PhotoSlot until a real people photo exists.

lead_magnet.title: The ADA parking walk-around
lead_magnet.subtitle: One page. Take it outside and look at your own lot.
value_stack: The number of accessible stalls your total stall count actually requires, in a table you can read in one pass
Van accessible stall and access aisle dimensions, with the mistakes that show up most often
Where the signs go, how high they mount and which ones your lot needs
Slope limits, and why a lot that passed ten years ago can fail today
The route from the accessible stall to your front door, which is where most lots actually fail
A walk-around you can hand to whoever opens the building in the morning
lead_magnet.consent_line: One checklist, sent once. It is not a subscription.
lead_magnet.content_gate: file is null. The PDF does not exist yet and the site withholds the block until it does. Every figure in it must be verified against the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design before it is written. Doctrine hard stop 1.
